solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great big character

definitions.meaning: great in the old-fashioned exclamatory sense of excellent, as in 'what a splendid idea'
an upper-case letter, the large form used at the start of a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: excellent as an exclamation, and an upper-case letter as opposed to a small one.

clue.text: Word uttered by shooter in Lancashire, say?

definitions.meaning: what a photographer asks people to say to make them smile for the camera
Lancashire is a crumbly English dairy product named after the county, so an example

explanation.walkthrough: 'shooter' suggests a gunman but is a photographer; Lancashire is a county in north-west England, and also gives its name to a crumbly white variety made there.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to say it so their lips form a smile, and Lancashire is one variety.

clue.text: Common for each vessel to carry four

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: to carry says the vessel holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Each ship carrying four crew is the usual arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread, found throughout everything, in the sense of prevalent.

clue.text: Complete collection of books in short story

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A complete set of books is contained in one short tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute or utter, as in a complete or utter disaster.

clue.text: One observing what's said by Irish across page in important article

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the article

parts.note: the leader is a newspaper's main editorial article

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the first piece spans the second

explanation.surface: An Irishman reads a page of the newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means Irish straddles the page; 'in' sets that inside the article. A leader is a British newspaper's editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person may follow speech by watching the speaker's mouth, observing what is said.

clue.text: Money went first — broke!

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, informal for money
led means went in front, went first

explanation.surface: Someone spent their cash too early and is now penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like the penniless sense hinted at by 'Money', but here it means gave way or collapsed under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gave way under pressure has collapsed, crumpled or folded, the verb sense of broke.

clue.text: Cook not half keen to open pub

indicators.note: to open says the piece goes inside, opening up the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word keen is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A chef is not especially eager to open a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half keen' reads like the British 'not half' meaning 'very', but it just halves the word; 'to open' sets that half in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes bread and cakes in an oven is a kind of cook.

clue.text: Fish key for chippy

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish
enter is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Fish is the key dish at a chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a chippy is a fish-and-chip shop, which 'Fish' plays on, but it is also slang for a woodworker, who makes chips of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a woodworker, from the wood chips the trade produces.

clue.text: Beast in the Andes before noon, everyone's seen climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going up the column, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Mountaineers in the Andes see an animal while climbing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly South American pack animal related to the camel, kept in the Andean highlands.

clue.text: Work under river — far down?

indicators.note: under says this piece sits below the other, coming after it in a down clue

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to ply is to work at, as in to ply a trade

explanation.surface: Engineers working beneath a river are a long way down.
explanation.definitionFit: At a great depth, an adverb for far below.

clue.text: Bird ends in cage, longing for the past

indicators.note: ends in tells us to take the final letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A caged bird pines for its former freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longing for the past' suggests REGRET, which is one letter off the answer, but the phrase is only there to supply final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This white wading heron is a species of bird.

clue.text: Work for peace to impress leader in kaiser, seeing inscrutable expression

indicators.note: to impress is to press something into a surface, so one letter is pressed inside the others
to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters of for peace are reshaped
the leader in a word is its first letter, here taken from kaiser

explanation.surface: Diplomats labour for peace while the Kaiser stays impossible to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to impress' puts K (the leader in 'kaiser') inside POERFACE, the anagram of FOR PEACE signalled by 'Work'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank face that reveals no feelings, as a card player keeps to hide the strength of a hand.

clue.text: Virtually nothing — a half?

definitions.meaning: something trivial or of little importance, next to nothing
in British pubs a half is a half-pint, a small measure of ale

explanation.walkthrough: A 'half' in a British pub is a half-pint, so it is literally a small quantity of ale; the question mark marks that playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a trivial matter, and a half-pint is literally a modest glass of ale.

clue.text: Communication from Anatolia, message to the west

indicators.note: to the west says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A message sent westward from Anatolia, the Asian part of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters sit inside 'Anatolia, message'. In an across clue, going west means reading right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a form of message or correspondence sent between computers.

clue.text: Member in state of uncertainty, briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: limbo is a state of being left undecided or in suspense

explanation.surface: A club member is left not knowing where they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or a leg is a member of the body, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Old leader getting on a bit, virtually bedbound?

indicators.note: bound means enclosed, so the shortened word surrounds the rest
virtually means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the word bed taken as written before shortening
taken as written
a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: An elderly leader, getting on a bit, is almost confined to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedbound' splits: 'virtually' trims the bed, and 'bound' has what is left enclose 'on a bit'. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, the French emperor, was a historical ruler, here a former head of state.

clue.text: Issue rejected after miserable break

indicators.note: after says the reversed piece comes behind the other one

parts.note: down means low in spirits, miserable

indicators.note: rejected says the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: A dejected worker's request for a holiday is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the issuing word round, and 'after' places it behind the word for miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of rest or inactivity away from work is a break.

clue.text: Supply of logs for festival

definitions.meaning: a stockpile of timber, a store of firewood
the famous 1969 rock music festival in New York State

explanation.definitionFit: A store of timber read as two words, and the celebrated 1969 open-air music festival.

clue.text: Must I talk about work while doing other chores?

indicators.note: about here means round and round, so the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they must talk about their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To juggle several tasks at once is to handle many jobs simultaneously.

clue.text: Painter: old one's recollection about retired artist

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the other piece
read as re-collection, gathering the letters together again in a new order
retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An elderly man reminisces about a painter who has given up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' is read as re-collection, a regathering of OLD ONE; 'about' wraps it round the artist, 'retired' turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci, the Renaissance master of the Mona Lisa, is a famous painter known by his first name.

clue.text: Part of Prospero, leading part

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Prospero, the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest, is the lead part in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's part in a play is the character they are cast to perform.

clue.text: Eton's principal in shock, seeing petition

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: the principal of a word is its leading, first letter

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Eton, Britain's famous public school, is shocked by a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea or formal request, the noun sense of petition.

clue.text: Bloke, one downing a plane perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a fellow or man, colloquial spelling of the word fellow
the plane is a tree, so this is a woodsman who cuts down trees

explanation.walkthrough: 'downing a plane' suggests shooting down an aircraft, but the plane is a tree, so it means cutting one down.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial spelling of fellow for a man, and also a person who cuts down trees.

clue.text: Build — from either side?

indicators.note: from either side says the letters read the same whichever end you start from

parts.note: to build is to erect, and the word for it is the one that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A builder can work on a structure from either side of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'from either side' is about the letters, which read the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure such as a shed or a fence is to build it.

clue.text: Standing on stool in field, get to the point?

indicators.note: standing in a down clue means set upright, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letters headed re
a cowpat is the stool left by cattle in a field

explanation.surface: Someone stands on a stool in a field to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stool' is not a seat but dung, so a cowpat in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow gradually to a thin end is to come to a point.

clue.text: Initial spin in action for batsman at Lord's?

definitions.meaning: a first trial run in a car before buying it

definitions.text: in action for batsman at Lord's?
definitions.meaning: a batsman in a Test match plays a drive, a forward attacking stroke

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, which hosts Test matches between national teams; a drive is a batting shot, so a Test batsman in action plays a test drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trial run in a vehicle before purchase is a spin, and Test cricket supplies the punning second sense.

clue.text: Minute to gulp new Aussie beer

indicators.note: to gulp is to swallow, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: minute means tiny

explanation.surface: An Australian takes a swift swallow of fresh ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a can of lager, from the metal container.

clue.text: Flipping ridiculous reptilian brain — you can say that again!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning ridiculous or excessive
the id is the primitive, instinctive part of the mind in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker scorns a crudely primitive brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but it signals the turn-round; the id is the instinctive self in Freud.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to mean the same again or I agree, used to echo a statement.

clue.text: Opera sent for translation — that's rarely understood

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, so the letters of opera sent are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: An opera is sent abroad to be translated because few follow its libretto.
explanation.definitionFit: The invented international language devised by Zamenhof has comparatively few fluent speakers.

clue.text: Track back around start of route

indicators.note: around says the first piece is placed round the second

parts.note: the tail is the back or rear end of something

indicators.note: start of says only the first letter of route is used

explanation.surface: A hiker retraces the path back near where the route began.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or a line of footprints is a track that can be followed.

clue.text: Gallery undergoing refurbishment, to a great extent

indicators.note: a refurbished building is reworked and rearranged, so the letters of gallery are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An art gallery is being extensively renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostly or for the most part, an adverb of degree.

clue.text: Rapper one criticises

definitions.meaning: a door fitting used to rap on the door to announce a visitor
someone who runs others down or finds fault, one who pans

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapper' wants to be a hip-hop musician; it is something that raps on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal ring on a front door raps, and a carping critic runs things down.
